## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Mechanistic considerations for targeted protein degradation vs. inhibition** [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/think-you-degrade)
  * Targeted protein degradation (TPD) offers a distinct pharmacological profile from occupancy-based small-molecule inhibitors by physically removing target proteins via cytosolic proteasomal pathways.
  * Efficacy and selectivity of TPD agents are highly contingent on target-specific baseline synthesis rates, intrinsic half-life, physiological clearance pathways, and target overexpression patterns in disease tissues.

* **TROP2 membrane localization ratio predicts datopotamab deruxtecan response in NSCLC** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04716-9)
  * Developed and validated a computational pathology biomarker—the TROP2 normalized membrane ratio—to quantify subcellular TROP2 localization in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
  * High TROP2 normalized membrane ratios were significantly associated with longer progression-free survival and overall survival in non-squamous NSCLC lacking actionable genomic alterations treated with datopotamab deruxtecan.

* **Renal STAT1/CEBPB axis identified as mediator of FGF23-induced inflammation in diabetic kidney disease** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.10.765607)
  * Single-nucleus RNA sequencing in mouse models of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) demonstrated that elevated circulating FGF23 acts through renal STAT1 and CEBPB transcription factor networks to promote inflammation under Klotho-deficient conditions.
  * Ex vivo targeting of CEBPB using the inhibitor ST-101 in precision-cut kidney slices attenuated FGF23-mediated pro-inflammatory gene expression.

* **Serum brain-derived tau differentiates acute TBI from spinal cord injury** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.08.26365143)
  * A multi-cohort evaluation (n = 342) demonstrated that baseline serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) concentrations accurately differentiate traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI) with an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87–0.96).
  * Paired sample analyses showed serum BD-tau outperformed CSF BD-tau for discriminating injury types (AUC = 0.95 vs. 0.80).

* **Adult body weight modifies lifespan extension efficacy in mouse models** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.10.765234)
  * Analysis of 33,780 mice in the Interventions Testing Program (ITP) demonstrated that geroprotective treatment efficacy scales positively with adult body weight in male mice (HR = 0.94 per SD weight increase).
  * Median lifespan extensions rose from 6.2% in the lowest weight quartile to 20.2% in the highest quartile across 13 of 14 tested compounds, primarily driven by accelerated mortality in heavier untreated controls.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **PepGen reports initial Phase 1/2 data for RNA therapeutic in myotonic dystrophy type 1** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/pepgen-myotonic-dystrophy-dm1-drug-results-freedom/874249/)
  * Early clinical readouts from the FREEDOM trial evaluating PepGen's oligonucleotide candidate demonstrated target engagement and splice-correction activity in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1).
  * Analyst updates noted favorable early delivery and safety profiles relative to competing clinical programs in development at Novartis and Dyne Therapeutics.

* **[Biotech]** **Nimbus Therapeutics initiates Phase 1 trial of SIK2 inhibitor** [LifeSciVC](https://lifescivc.com/2026/11/molecules-to-medicines-the-pursuit-of-repeatable-drug-discovery/)
  * Dosed the first participant in a first-in-human Phase 1 clinical trial evaluating NDI-225673, an oral, highly selective salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2) inhibitor.
  * NDI-225673 is being developed for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases following successful completion of GLP toxicology studies.

* **Surv-Targeted peptide vaccine OVM-200 shows safety and immunogenicity in Phase 1 trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.08.26367556)
  * Open-label Phase 1 evaluation (n = 27) of OVM-200, a cathepsin S-cleavable overlapping peptide vaccine targeting survivin (BIRC5), met its primary safety endpoint in patients with advanced NSCLC, ovarian, or prostate cancer.
  * OVM-200 induced survivin-specific T-cell responses with only Grade 1–2 adverse events and no dose-limiting toxicities.

* **Brepocitinib evaluated in Phase 2 trial for cutaneous sarcoidosis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43008126/)
  * Completed a Phase 2 double-blind randomized clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of the oral dual TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor brepocitinib in patients with cutaneous sarcoidosis.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Adalimumab fails to improve outcomes following needle fasciotomy for Dupuytren contracture** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43007834/)
  * A randomized controlled pilot trial showed that post-operative administration of TNF inhibitor adalimumab provided no significant improvement in clinical outcomes compared to standard care following needle fasciotomy.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Biotech]** **Beam Therapeutics base editing candidate risto-cel meets primary endpoint in pivotal trial** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/beam-sickle-cell-base-editing-risto-cel-results/874242/)
  * Pivotal trial results for risto-cel (an autologous base-edited cell therapy targeting gamma-globin gene promoters) met primary efficacy and safety endpoints in severe sickle cell disease.
  * Beam announced plans to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the US FDA as early as late 2026.

* **Adjunctive Saccharomyces boulardii reduces H. pylori eradication efficacy in randomized trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.09.26367596)
  * A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n = 218) tested 14-day *S. boulardii* adjunctive therapy alongside PPI, bismuth, amoxicillin, and clarithromycin quadruple therapy in a high-resistance setting.
  * Per-protocol analysis revealed significantly lower *H. pylori* eradication rates in the *S. boulardii* group compared to placebo (65.0% vs. 76.5%; RR = 0.849, 95% CI: 0.72–0.99).

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-pimicotinib-symptomatic-tenosynovial-giant-cell-tumor)
  * The FDA approved pimicotinib (Pimjetmi, EMD Serono), an oral CSF-1R kinase inhibitor, for adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) ineligible for surgical resection due to morbidity risk.
  * Approval was supported by the Phase 3 MANEUVER trial (NCT05804045), showing statistically significant improvements in overall response rate (ORR) by independent central review versus placebo.

* **First factor XIa inhibitor approved by FDA for stroke prevention** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00180-9)
  * The FDA granted approval to the first factor XIa inhibitor indicated for secondary stroke prevention, establishing a new therapeutic class designed to mitigate thrombosis without disrupting baseline hemostasis.

* **[Biotech]** **Grail targets early Q1 2027 FDA approval decision for Galleri test** [X (formerly Twitter)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120196167262929083)
  * Grail expects a regulatory decision from the FDA regarding approval of its Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood test by early Q1 2027.
  * The company anticipates an initial reimbursement rate setting between $500 and $600 per test.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca acquires conjugate vaccine technology developer Omniose** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/glp1-naion-compass-zura-abeona/874076/)
  * AstraZeneca acquired preclinical biotech Omniose to integrate its bacterial bioconjugation platform into its pipeline, targeting simplified production of bacterial conjugate vaccines.

* **[Biotech]** **Oura acquires clinical AI firm Counsel Health for $625 million** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/oura-acquires-counsel-health-big-bet-ai-care/)
  * Smart ring maker Oura agreed to acquire Counsel Health, a clinical generative AI startup, in a transaction valued at $625 million to expand direct-to-consumer clinical decision support capabilities.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Former Eli Lilly sales representative files lawsuit over Mounjaro promotion** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/10/former-lilly-rep-claims-she-was-fired-for-complaining-about-marketing-of-mounjaro-diabetes-drug/)
  * A lawsuit filed against Eli Lilly alleges wrongful termination of a sales representative after she raised internal compliance objections regarding off-label marketing of Mounjaro (tirzepatide) for weight loss prior to its dedicated obesity approval.

* **[Biotech]** **Prime Medicine prices $125 million public offering** [X (formerly Twitter)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2120354929038790683)
  * Prime Medicine announced the pricing of an underwritten public offering of common stock totaling $125 million at a price of $3.50 per share.

## Public Health & Policy

* **US risks losing WHO measles elimination status** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/11/health-news-us-may-soon-lose-measles-elimination-status/)
  * The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO/WHO) convened to evaluate whether continuous domestic transmission of measles over 12 months will cause the US to lose its official disease elimination status maintained since 2000.

* **Infant bleeding cases surge following increases in parental vitamin K refusal** [Science-Based Medicine](http://sciencebasedmedicine.org/vitamin-k-refusal-and-infant-bleeding-surge/)
  * Two studies published in *JAMA* journals documented a rise in preventable infant vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) cases, directly linked to growing rates of parental refusal of newborn intramuscular vitamin K injections.

* **Congressional Democrats open inquiry into executive Most-Favored-Nation drug pricing deals** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/democrats-investigate-most-favored-nation-deals-letters-drugmakers/)
  * Committee leaders in the US Congress requested documentation from pharmaceutical manufacturers concerning Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) drug pricing agreements executed during the prior administration.

* **Calls for mandatory independent oversight following gene-editing trial fatalities in China** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04768-x)
  * Analysis of safety events and patient deaths in investigator-initiated cell and gene therapy trials in China emphasizes critical gaps in local institutional protocol oversight, advocating for standardized external safety monitoring boards.

* **DoxyPEP deployment generates population-level indirect protection against STIs** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.21.26358607)
  * Implementation of doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxyPEP) among 9% of high-risk MSM and transgender women led to a 80% reduction in chlamydia and 65% reduction in syphilis among recipients.
  * Non-recipient MSM/TGW within the same sexual networks experienced indirect protection, with chlamydia and syphilis rates dropping 41% and 29%, respectively.

***

**Worth watching:** **Beam Therapeutics**' pending BLA filing for risto-cel will mark the first regulatory submission for an *in vivo* or autologous *ex vivo* base-editing therapeutic platform.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Even 99% AI Accuracy Isn't Enough in Healthcare](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/sEN8YE7Tses) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Stephanie Davis explains why AI tools developed for clinicians require rigorous clinical vetting before implementation.
        - Emphasizes that even a small risk of AI hallucination or a 1% error rate can lead to severe consequences in healthcare.
        - Highlights the critical importance of safety protocols and human supervision when deploying clinical digital health tools.
    - [Why So Many Doctors Want to Leave Medicine](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/aX9B8gWD_X8) -- Health2Tech
        - Alison Curfman addresses the systemic issues behind widespread physician burnout in healthcare.
        - Identifies operational burdens such as late-night administrative charting as key factors depriving doctors of family time.
        - Explains how these chronic pressures prompt overwhelmed medical professionals to pursue early retirement or alternative careers.
- Pure Science
    - [Why you can't trust a test that's 99% accurate](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2QSkkhbl3v4) -- Veritasium
        - Explores the mathematical implications behind interpreting positive results on diagnostic medical tests.
        - Demonstrates why receiving a positive result on a 99% accurate test does not necessarily mean an individual has the disease.
        - Addresses how test accuracy metrics interact with real-world probability and diagnosis reliability.
- Other
    - [Crash Course World History Marathon • Full Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EQr_eJOFy4Q) -- CrashCourse
        - Consolidates the complete 42-episode Crash Course World History series into a long-form marathon video.
        - Covers major historical eras and topics ranging from the Agricultural Revolution and ancient empires to the Industrial Revolution, world wars, and globalization.
        - Served as part of Complexly's annual Learn-a-Thon initiative to provide accessible educational content.
